item.title: Expansion, sourcing gains ahead for JSW Steel as capacity and volumes rise
item.description: JSW Steel plans to expand capacity to 78 million tonnes by FY32, backed by raw material integration, stronger volumes and internal cash flows, though coking coal costs remain a concern.
item.dc:creator: Devangshu Datta
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Expansion, sourcing gains ahead for JSW Steel as capacity and volumes rise

Expansion, sourcing gains ahead for JSW Steel as capacity and volumes rise JSW Steel plans to expand capacity to 78 million tonnes by FY32, backed by raw material integration, stronger volumes and internal cash flows, though coking coal costs remain a concern. premium

JSW Steel plans to expand its capacity to 78 million tonnes by FY32, supported by higher production volumes, raw material integration and internal cash flows. (Photo: Reuters)

Devangshu Datta New Delhi 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 28 2026 | 5:57 PM IST

Listen to This Article

JSW Steel (JSTL) has followed a consistent strategy of capacity expansion, while also working to secure sourcing of coal, iron ore and coking coal, among others.

Q2FY27 results were in line with consensus, and the company reiterated its capital expenditure (capex) commitment and guidance.

Backward integration involves tying up coking coal from Mozambique and Australia (for about 15 million tonnes per annum or mtpa), as well as setting up washeries, and sourcing from captive iron ore mines which will cover 50 per cent of requirement.

The upstream portfolio is expanding to include speciality products like cold-rolled grain-oriented (CRGO) steel, cold-rolled non-oriented electrical (CRNO), tinplate, bearing steel, alloy steel, rails and so on.

Assured raw material and more blast furnace capacity should improve operating leverage and enhance cost competitiveness. Steel is expected to have a long upcycle, given demand created by long-term public capex commitment to infrastructure.

JSTL is looking to capture the realisation upside and grow volumes also. The management expects domestic demand to grow 7-8 per cent in FY27. Steel consumption rose 7 per cent Y-o-Y in Q2FY27 and 7.5 per cent in H1FY27. The FY27 production and sales guidance is maintained at 29.75 million tonnes (mt) and 28.6 mt, respectively (excluding JSW-JFE Steel).

The transfer of Bhushan Power & Steel (BPSL) to JFE JV via a slump sale effective March 2026 means ex-BPSL pro forma must be used for adjusted year-on-year (Y-o-Y) calculations. The Q2FY27 earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) of ₹10,120 crore, was up 7.9 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q), with 19.3 per cent Q-o-Q volume growth.

But realisations were pulled down by higher coking coal costs. Compared to adjusted ex-BPSL pro forma for Q2FY26, volumes grew 13 per cent Y-o-Y.

Net debt reduced to ₹44,500 crore, down ₹1,680 crore Q-o-Q, due to the slump sale. JSTL repaid a $500 million bond in October 2026 ahead of maturity (April 2027). Dollar exposure declined from over $6 billion in Q1FY26 to $3.5-3.6 billion. The net debt/Ebitda ratio dropped to 1.28 times from 1.46 times in Q1FY27. JSTL’s capex was ₹11,100 crore in H1FY27 and the company reiterated its FY27 capex guidance of ₹22,000 crore-₹24,000 crore.

The management says JSTL generates cash (around ₹25,000 crore-₹30,000 crore per annum) to maintain capex and reduce debt. Price support will also come from safeguard duty.

There was a $10 per tonne increase in coking coal costs in Q2FY27, which was below the guidance of $12-15 per tonne of anticipated increase. Hence, Ebitda/tonne declined by ₹1,442 Q-o-Q to ₹13,566 per tonne. Adjusted Ebitda per tonne (ex-BPSL) was ₹13,326 per tonne, down 11 per cent Q-o-Q but up 24 per cent Y-o-Y, ex-BPSL pro forma, due to higher coking coal prices.

Higher volumes drove profits. Production and sales volumes increased to 7.3 mt and 7.5 mt, respectively, from 6.6 mt and 6.3 mt in Q1FY27, due to Vijayanagar blast furnace-3 operating at 90 per cent utilisation.

Lower debt makes it easier to fund capex. JSTL has accelerated expansion, pushing the capex budget to ₹1.48 trillion over 5-6 years. The management expects expenditure to mostly be funded through internal accruals.

Steel capacity will rise from 38 mt in FY26 to 44 mt (FY28) and to 65 mt (FY31) and 78 mt by FY32. The management believes there will be no balance sheet stress during the capex period even if steel prices are low, given projected cashflows.

Production volumes will be strong in Q3FY27, driven by Vijayanagar BF-3 and JSW Vijayanagar Metallics (JVML) operating at full capacity. JSTL can meet its FY27 guidance, though high coking coal costs will compress margins.

Coking coal prices are expected to rise by $25/mt in Q3. But JSTL believes margin will improve due to steel price increases and efficiency gains. The like-for-like volume growth is guided at 8 per cent for FY27.

Comparing with adjusted ex-BPSL for Q2FY26, Q2FY27 revenue was ₹54,500 crore, up 31 per cent Y-o-Y (15 per cent Q-o-Q). The adjusted Ebitda was ₹9,940 crore, up 39 per cent Y-o-Y, comparing ex-BPSL, and up 6 per cent Q-o-Q, due to higher volumes. Adjusted net profit was ₹5,100 crore (up 10 per cent Q-o-Q).

Consolidated average selling prices (ASP) was ₹73,000/tonne (t) (₹75,780/t in Q1FY27 and ₹62,640/t (ex-BPSL) in Q2FY26).

Steel prices recovered at Q2-end as monsoon eased. Price hikes in October after price recovery through August-September 2026 will be reflected in Q3 realisations. Iron ore costs were a little higher in Q2FY27. Ore costs may be marginally higher in Q3FY27, but prices could soften as supply bottlenecks ease. Long steel prices look to be healthy in H2FY27, and flat prices recovered in Q2FY27.

Better fixed cost absorption will come with volume expansion. The valuations seem reasonable. Integration across the value chain will stabilise margins. But this is an ambitious expansion plan and downturns in the steel cycle could impact projections.

item.title: JPMorgan to lead US retail offering in Anthropic's potential record IPO
item.description: The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ryan Gould and Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC has tapped JPMorgan Chase & Co. to lead US sales of shares to individual investors in its potentially record-setting initial public offering, people familiar with the matter said. The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall, some of the people said. JPMorgan Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the Wall Street bank’s campaign, one of them added. JPMorgan is reprising its role leading the effort to gather retail orders for SpaceX’s $86.2 billion IPO, which saw more than $100 billion of demand from individual investors, Bloomberg News has reported.  Citigroup Inc. is set to coordinate the international retail offering, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Anthropic’s IPO includes offerings in Australia, Canada, Japan, certain European Economic Area countries, Switzerland and the UK, according to the IPO filing. JPMorgan is coordinating outreach on Anthropic’s IPO to high-net-worth investors and private banking clients as well as broker platforms, the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the share of the offering earmarked for retail could change, the people said. Representatives for Anthropic, JPMorgan and Citigroup declined to comment. Anthropic filed publicly on Monday for an IPO that would see it and some of its investors sell shares, marking the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering. Investors are telling bankers on the deal that their estimate of a fair valuation has shifted to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion, though a valuation of closer to $1.75 trillion is potentially achievable, Bloomberg News has reported. The amount of money needed to fund the development of AI and its associated infrastructure has spurred companies to raise tens of billions of dollars at a time.  Meta Platforms Inc. on Monday kicked off a plan to raise as much as $98 billion in equity, which would be one of the largest financing exercises of its kind in history. It follows Google parent Alphabet Inc.’s $85 billion equity fundraising plan earlier this year. Anthropic and rival OpenAI are seeking to raise record amounts while facing mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents.

Tata Projects secures order from GSFC for acid complex in Gujarat The proposed complex will comprise a 600 metric tonnes per day (MTPD) phosphoric acid plant and a 1,800 metric tonnes per day (MTPD) sulphuric acid plant

The contract marks an important milestone in Tata Projects' expansion into specialised process industries and reinforces its position as an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) partner for complex industrial infrastructure | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 28 2026 | 3:21 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Tata Projects, the country's leading technology-led engineering, procurement and construction company, on Wednesday said that it has secured an order from Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd (GSFC) to develop an integrated phosphoric acidsulphuric acid complex in Gujarat. The contract marks an important milestone in Tata Projects' expansion into specialised process industries and reinforces its position as an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) partner for complex industrial infrastructure. The proposed complex will comprise a 600 metric tonnes per day (MTPD) phosphoric acid plant and a 1,800 metric tonnes per day (MTPD) sulphuric acid plant, along with associated utilities and offsite infrastructure. "Tata Projects... has secured a significant EPC contract from Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Limited for the development of an integrated Phosphoric AcidSulphuric Acid (PASA) complex at Sikka, Jamnagar, Gujarat," the company said in a statement.

The project entails setting up integrated phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid manufacturing facilities, along with the required utilities and offsite infrastructure, it said. Also Read

"As we expand our presence in chemicals, fertilisers and other specialised process industries, our priority remains to build a high-quality, diversified order book anchored in technical expertise, execution credibility and enduring customer partnerships," Rajiv Menon, President & Chief Growth & Strategy Officer, Tata Projects, said. Tata Projects has expertise in providing sustainable solutions for the execution of large and complex urban and industrial infrastructure projects while also demonstrating a strong presence in refineries and petrochemical plants. It provides ready-to-deploy solutions for semiconductor facilities, giga factories, data centres, refineries, green fuels, roads, bridges, integrated rail & metro systems, commercial buildings and airports, power generation, transmission and distribution systems, chemical process plants, water and waste management, and mining and metal purification systems.

item.title: Infosys draws four downgrades in a day on weaker annual sales outlook
item.description: Brokerages turn cautious as Infosys' reduced FY27 sales guidance raises concerns over demand recovery and AI-led disruption ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Faseeh Mangi Infosys Ltd. was downgraded by at least four analysts in a single day after India’s second-largest software exporter cut its annual sales forecast, deepening concerns over disruption from artificial intelligence. Axis Capital Ltd., Arihant Capital Markets Ltd., and IIFL Capital Services Ltd. were among brokerages that lowered their ratings on Monday, data compiled by Bloomberg show. Three others reduced their recommendations over the weekend, pushing its consensus rating to 3.7 out of 5, the lowest since January 2024. The downgrades for the sector’s bellwether threatens to derail a nascent recovery in India’s battered technology shares. The Nifty IT Index is on track for its best month since July, even as concerns mount over soaring debt levels being used to fund the global AI buildout.  Infosys cutting its annual sales forecast signals that a broad-based recovery in IT budgets has yet to materialize. Revenue will rise 1% to 2% on a constant-currency basis in the year through March 2027, the company said late Friday, versus analysts’ estimates of just over 2%.  India’s $280 billion-plus software services industry has been grappling with a slowdown, with companies limiting spending in the midst of geopolitical crises such as the Iran conflict, surging energy prices and elevated inflation.  Infosys shares have fallen 28% this year on ongoing concerns about its ability to weather AI disruption. The average target price from 44 analysts is 1,200 rupees. The stock tumbled about 3% to 1,132.2 rupees in early trading on Tuesday.
